questions.problem: Expressed in terms of ${log}_{4}$, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${4}^{x+1}={7}^{x}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{4}$ in both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{x+1} & ={7}^{x} \\ {log}_{4}⁡({4}^{x+1}) & ={log}_{4}⁡({7}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{4}⁡({4}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & ={log}_{4}⁡({7}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & ={log}_{4}⁡({7}^{x}) \\ x+1 & =x{log}_{4}⁡(7)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =x{log}_{4}⁡(7) \\ x-x{log}_{4}⁡(7) & =-1 \\ x(1-{log}_{4}⁡(7)) & =-1 \\ x & =-\frac{1}{1-{log}_{4}⁡(7)}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{10}^{x+1} & ={2}^{x} \\ \operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{x+1}) & =\operatorname{log}⁡({2}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x+1=\operatorname{log}⁡({2}^{x})
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
x+1=x\operatorname{log}⁡(2)
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$

questions.problem: Given that ${5}^{y}={4}^{y+1},$ what is the value of $y?$ Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{5}$ on both sides of the equation: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{y}={4}^{y+1} \\ {log}_{5}⁡({5}^{y}) & ={log}_{5}⁡({4}^{y+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={log}_{5}⁡({4}^{y+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =(y+1){log}_{5}⁡4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $y,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =(y+1){log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y & =y{log}_{5}⁡4+{log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y-y{log}_{5}⁡4 & ={log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y(1-{log}_{5}⁡4) & ={log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y & =\frac{{log}_{5}⁡4}{1-{log}_{5}⁡4}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the change of base formula, we have

$$
{log}_{5}⁡(4)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}≈0.861\,353.
$$

Finally, then, we can approximate $y$ as

$$
\begin{aligned}y≈\frac{0.861\,353}{1-0.861\,353}≈6.213,\end{aligned}
$$

to $3$ decimal places.

questions.problem: Expressed in terms of common logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${10}^{x-3}={7}^{x}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the common logarithm $(log)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{10}^{x-3} & ={7}^{x} \\ \operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{x-3}) & =\operatorname{log}⁡({7}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & =\operatorname{log}⁡({7}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & =x\operatorname{log}⁡(7)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-x\operatorname{log}⁡(7) & =3 \\ x(1-\operatorname{log}⁡(7)) & =3 \\ x & =\frac{3}{1-\operatorname{log}⁡(7)}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Exact Solutions of Exponential Equations
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{8}$ on both sides of the equation: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{8}^{1-x} & ={3}^{x/2} \\ {log}_{8}⁡({8}^{1-x}) & ={log}_{8}⁡({3}^{x/2})\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side:

$$
1-x={log}_{8}⁡({3}^{x/2})
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
1-x=\frac{x}{2}{log}_{8}⁡3
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}1-x & =\frac{x}{2}{log}_{8}⁡3 \\ 1 & =x+\frac{x}{2}{log}_{8}⁡3 \\ x+\frac{x}{2}{log}_{8}⁡3 & =1 \\ 2x+x{log}_{8}⁡3 & =2 \\ x(2+{log}_{8}⁡3) & =2 \\ x & =\frac{2}{2+{log}_{8}⁡3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the change of base formula, we have

$$
{log}_{8}⁡(3)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}≈0.528\,321.
$$

Finally,  we can approximate $x$ as 

$$
x≈\frac{2}{2+0.528\,321}≈0.791,
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

questions.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $y$ satisfies the equation ${e}^{y}={8}^{1-2y}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{y} & ={8}^{1-2y} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({8}^{1-2y})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡({8}^{1-2y})
$$

Finally, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
y=(1-2y)\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)
$$

Finally, we solve for $y$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =(1-2y)\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)-2y\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ y+2y\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ y(1+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ y & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}{1+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{y+1} & ={3}^{2y} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y+1}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{2y})\end{aligned}

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
y+1=\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{2y})\,
$$

Next, we use the power and product laws of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
y+1=2y\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)
$$

Finally, we solve for $y$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y+1 & =2y\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ 2y\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-y & =1 \\ y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-1) & =1 \\ y & =\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-1}\end{aligned}

questions.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${e}^{x-3}={5}^{x+1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x-3} & ={5}^{x+1} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x-3}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x-3=\operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x+1})
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
x-3=(x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡5
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & =(x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x-3 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡5+\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡5+3 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡5+3 \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5+3}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives

$$
2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)=(x-7)\operatorname{ln}⁡(10).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =(x-7)\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) \\ 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) \\ 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) & =-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =7\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)) & =7\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) \\ x & =\frac{7\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}\end{aligned}

canonical_examples.problem: Expressed in terms of $\log_2,$ what value of $x$ satisfies the equation $2^{x+1}=3^x?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we take $\log_2$ on both sides of the equation: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{x+1} & ={3}^{x} \\ {log}_{2}⁡({2}^{x+1}) & ={log}_{2}⁡({3}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\log_b \left( b^c \right) = c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x+1 = \log_2 \left(3^{x}\right)
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
x+1 = x \log_2 \left(3\right)
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =x{log}_{2}⁡(3) \\ x{log}_{2}⁡(3)-x & =1 \\ x({log}_{2}⁡(3)-1) & =1 \\ x & =\frac{1}{{log}_{2}⁡(3)-1}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation $e^{x+1}=2^x\cdot 5?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x+1} & ={2}^{x}\cdot 5 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x+1}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x}\cdot 5)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\ln \left( e^a \right) = a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x+1 =\ln \left(2^{x}\cdot 5\right)
$$

Next, we use the power and product laws of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x+1 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-1 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-1 \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-1}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, determine the value of $x$ that satisfies the equation $5^{x+2}=9^{x-2}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{x+2} & ={9}^{x-2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x+2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({9}^{x-2})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives

$$
(x+2)\ln(5) = (x-2)\ln(9).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+2)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =(x-2)\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) & =-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)) & =2(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)) \\ x & =\frac{2(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(9))}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\end{aligned}
$$
